title: Use a list as a small queue
summary: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour.
introduction: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour. Your task: Pop the next item and predict its value.
learningObjectives: Pop the next item and predict its value.
Explain the example for use a list as a small queue

blocks.text: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour.
Use a local Redis server and redis-cli. Commands here use cma: practice keys only. Redis commands do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Do not connect these exercises to a production database.

blocks.code:
DEL cma:queue
RPUSH cma:queue "Moon Trip" "Garden Days"
LPOP cma:queue
blocks.title: Use a list as a small queue

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `RPUSH` adds values at the right end of a Redis list. Pairing it with LPOP gives a simple first-in, first-out queue.

blocks.text: The removed value is Moon Trip, the first item added.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This simple pop queue can lose a job if a worker fails after taking it. Reliable job systems need more design.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Pop the next item and predict its value.
